title: Where is the centre of rotation of a square?
description: A square gets back onto itself after a ninety degree turn, and the point it turns about has to be found. The centre of rotation is the middle point, where the two diagonals meet. Keeko's doubt is that the pin can go at any corner.
teaching_notes: One idea: the turning point of a square is the middle point, equally far from all four corners, where the diagonals cross. Watch for students who place the pin on a corner.

source: A square gets back onto itself after a 90� rotation. Do you
video_script.why: The child sees that the point a square turns about must be equally far from all four corners, so it is the middle point where the diagonals cross.
video_script.substitution: Try a pin at different points, and keep the point that lets the square land on itself after a quarter turn.
video_script.anchor: a square with a pin through one point and the two diagonals drawn faintly
video_script.wrong_answer: the pin can go at any corner
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the pin can go at any corner. With the pin at a corner, a quarter turn swings the other corners round it and the square lands in a different place, so it does not fit its start picture. Only the middle point keeps the square on itself.
video_script.payoff_line: The centre of rotation is the point where the two diagonals cross

final_answer.value: At the centre of the square, the point where its two diagonals cross
final_answer.spoken: the centre of rotation is the middle point of the square

never_show: a pin at a corner as the right answer
maths_rules: When a shape turns, one point stays fixed; this fixed point is called the centre of rotation
A line joining two opposite corners of a square is called a diagonal
In a quarter turn the four corners swap places, so the turning point is equally far from all four corners
The two diagonals of a square meet at the middle point, which is equally far from all four corners
A pin at a corner leaves the square in a different place after a quarter turn, so a corner is not the centre of rotation
video_script.design: One idea: the centre of rotation of a square is the middle point where the diagonals meet. The square stays on the board all video. Wrong idea: the pin can go at any corner.
